extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, law students, and practitioners in patent litigation and prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: An index-style compilation of substantive legal standards, criteria, and procedures across patent law (validity, infringement, remedies, procedure, Patent Office practice). Useful for evaluating patentability, infringement, remedies, reissue/extension, and related litigation defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-Office extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory foundation and procedures for extensions; applications for extensions; when extensions are grantable; how certified; inventor's rights in extensions; operation on existing specimens; proceedings on applications; repeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subentries: statutory foundation of extensions; applications for extensions; grantable when; certified how; inventor's rights; operation on existing specimens of the invention; proceedings on applications for extensions; repeal of extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faults which call for disclaimers / reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Faults in a patent that require disclaimers and faults that render patents reissuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index references to faults leading to disclaimers (193, 194) and faults causing reissuability (218); includes inadvertence and mistake as causes (see 'Inadvertence', 'Mistake').

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees (taxable costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys', clerks', commissioners', witness fees and which are taxable as costs in patent litigation and Patent Office practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted items: attorneys' fees taxable as costs; clerks' fees; commissioners' fees; witness fees; references to first and final Patent Office fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form as affecting questions of infringement and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of an article affects both infringement and invention inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index points to how changes in form affect infringement questions (363-368) and invention questions (41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements of patents and applications and how letters can evidence compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters as evidence of compliance with formal requisites (491); formalities of application and execution referenced elsewhere (e.g., Letters Patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud in obtaining patents or extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraud in procuring or granting patents or Patent-Office extensions and remedies for such fraud; selling patents by means of fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes action for procuring a patent on another invention, fraud in granting/procuring letters patent or extensions, remedies for fraud in obtaining patents/extensions/reissues, and selling patents by means of fraud (references 321, 321-323, 284).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions (as related to equivalents and claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functionality considered in determining equivalents and identity of an invention; functions may be stated in claims and performed substantially the same way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoints: functions considered in respect of equivalents (352); difference of function consistent with identity (180a); performed in substantially the same way (353); stated in claims (117a, 176, 183, 220).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign country / prior art effects
rubrics_metrics.description: How foreign acts, publications, knowledge, or sales affect novelty, prior use, and constructive abandonment for U.S. patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conception of invention in foreign country (141a); infringement by sale in foreign country (707, 708); prior knowledge or use in foreign country prior to patentee's invention (54); printed publication or public use/sale in foreign country more than two years prior to the patentee's application (104a, 101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Patent (effects on novelty and abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of foreign patent applications or grants on novelty and constructive abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: foreign patent application operating toward constructive abandonment (104a); operation on novelty (54, 55); operation to constructive abandonment (104a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Forfeiture principles in patent law (not favored) and forfeiture of licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forfeiture is not favored in law (108); forfeiture of licenses references (308, 309).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of judge when trying action at law without a jury
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and effect of a judge's findings in non-jury trials in patent actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to when judge's finding governs (540) and related procedures for jury vs judge questions elsewhere (instructions, review).

rubrics_metrics.name: "For the Purpose Set Forth" (claim language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and interpretation of the phrase 'for the purpose set forth' within a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed under the nature of the phrase in claims (182); used in claim construction analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities of Letters Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Constituents, formalities, construction, presumption, duration, and evidentiary effect of letters patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive subguidance: addressed to those skilled in the art (174); letters as contracts (189); construed liberally where appropriate (185) and narrowly if not used (185); construed in light of inventor's acts, contemporaneous construction, Patent Office restrictions, expert testimony, state of the art; prima facie evidence of validity (491); formalities of execution (121, 122); duration and territorial extent (160-163, 707). Also how errors and vague descriptions affect validity and how letters patent are proved (129, 506).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement (general principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple facets of infringement: types (making, using, selling), damages and profits, proof and evidence, cessation, contributory infringement, design/mechanical/composition/process specifics, and how questions are affected by changes to form, substitution of equivalents, or mode of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subentries include infringement by making/selling/using; damages for making (564), making+selling (561), selling (563); profits (717-724, 724, 725-734); proof of infringement and evidence to disprove (497-501, 532); contributory infringement (404-407); effect of changes: addition, change of form (363-368), substitution of equivalents (350, 370-371), omission (349, 369), rearrangement (348), results (340), mode of operation (341-346), manufacture before patent issued (158), etc. Also procedural items: how stated in bills and declarations (579, 434-435), proof on motions for preliminary injunctions (676).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions (preliminary and permanent standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preliminary and permanent injunctions in patent cases: required proofs, defences, timing, scope, bonds, hearings, appeal effects, and when injunctions will or will not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive subguidance: proof of complainant's title and proof of infringement/danger necessary (675-676); preliminary injunctive relief based on danger of infringement/irreparable injury (676); relative benefits of parties considered (670); defences that avert injunctions include estoppel, laches, license, proof patent void or expired, acquiescence (679-684); injunctions not granted for trivial infringements, to restrain third-party suits, or to restrain issuance of letters patent (705, 134); bonds pending motions (663); description in preliminary (702); duration, suspension pending appeal, dissolution and motions to dissolve (659-707, 692-695, 696a-703); territorial scope (707); injunctions to restrain unauthorized marking (333).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interferences (procedure and substantive standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and standards governing interference proceedings: definition, burden of proof, comparative dates, conception and reduction to practice, disclosure, drawings/models, estoppel, evidence, decisions, and interlocutory effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subentries: defined (140); burden of proof in interferences (141); comparative dates (141a, 141b); conception and reduction to practice (141a, 141b, 141c); disclosure/drawings/models in interferences (141a, 141c); estoppel and laches in interferences; evidence and rules of evidence (141, 141a-c); decisions in interference and their use as foundation for preliminary injunctions (674).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity (of inventions and applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree and proof of identity between applications, patents, and reissues relevant to constructive abandonment, novelty, and litigation pleadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoints: degree of identity in constructive abandonment (98); in novelty (62); how lack of identity between application and patent is pleaded in actions at law and in equity and how proved (various sections 450, 514, 459, 524, 460, 525); presence of identity between several patents to one inventor and how tested (180a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignorance and its (irrelevant) effect on novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignorance of anticipating matter does not avert negation of novelty; ignorance of letters patent does not avert judgment for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index references: ignorance of anticipating matter (73) and of letters patent (377, 569); rules on what public knowledge must include to negative novelty (72).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement (patentable subject and relation to invention/infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements may be subjects of patents but may or may not constitute invention and may or may not infringe existing patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subentries: improvement a subject of a patent (1); may/may not be invention (16); may/may not infringe (376); sorts of improvement (16, 285).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertence, Accident, and Mistake (relating to reissues and disclaimers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadvertence/accident/mistake can cause necessity for disclaimers or render patents reissuable; absence of inadvertence/accident/mistake and how proved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index references: inadvertence causing disclaimers and reissuable faults (193, 218); absence of inadvertence/accident/mistake how proved (522); mistake justifying disclaimers (195-196); remedy for issuing patents through mistake (321).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of defendant's device (discovery/inspection standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: When inspection of defendant's accused device is permitted in patent litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to inspection permitted (636); relates to evidentiary practice and interlocutory procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions to juries (in patent trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for jury instructions: what must be embodied in writing, exceptions, review standards, and what instructions must embody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexes: instructions to be given in writing (537); exceptions to instructions (553, 554); how instructions are reviewed (552); what instructions must embody (537).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest on damages and profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Accrual of interest on damages and on profits recovered in patent cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed references: interest on damages (571); interest on profits (736); relevant to remedies and accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity (causes and relation to reissue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple causes of invalidity and when invalidity constitutes a cause for reissuability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eighteen causes of invalidity cited (440, 441); when invalidity is a cause of reissuability (216).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention (standards for patentable invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes invention versus mere aggregation, duplication, change in degree, omission, substitution of equivalents, workmanship, or mere skill; evidence relevant to invention and dates of conception/reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoints: absent from mere aggregation (32), change in degree (31), mere duplication (34), enlargement (30), omission of parts (35), substitution of equivalents (36), substitution of superior materials (28), union of parts making one (35), new/analogous use of old process not invention (38), product of mere skill not invention (25), conception/disclosure/drawings/models evidence, mechanical simplicity relevance (26, 42), grades of invention (22), necessary to patentability (23), dates of invention and proof (69, 70, 510).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Infringement / Joint Infringers
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for when joint acts constitute infringement, recovery for joint infringers, contribution between joint infringers, releases, and pleading issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: facts constituting joint infringement (407); profits recoverable in joint infringement (712); recovery for separate acts in suits against joint infringers (406); contribution and releases among joint infringers (531).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Invention / Joint Patent (effects and pleading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between joint and sole invention; effects of joint invention on validity; how to plead and prove joint invention or joint patent in law and equity; when joint patent voids sole patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subentries: joint invention distinguished from sole invention (45, 46); distinguished from suggestions to sole inventor (47); for sole patent, how pleaded and proved in actions at law/equity (452, 605, 516-517); joint patent for sole invention may void patent (50-51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction (of courts and Patent Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdictional rules relevant to patent suits: federal courts, state courts, equity jurisdiction, Commissioner authority to grant reissues/extensions, Court of Claims and courts of first resort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoints: consent may confer jurisdiction (389); jurisdiction in interference, qui tam actions; objections to jurisdiction waived by general appearance (389); Commissioner of Patents' jurisdiction to grant extensions and reissues (266, 211-221); jurisdiction of District Courts over suits against government agents (93); Court of Claims jurisdiction (391-392); equity jurisdiction where patent expired since bill filed (592).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury Trials and Judges' roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Division of questions between judge and jury in patent cases and procedures for non-jury trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries reference jury instructions and what questions are for juries (499, 500, 537); judges decide questions of construction (189, 499, 500); trying actions in equity with juries (642); judge findings when trying without jury (540).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laches (equitable defense)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laches as a defense in equity and to preliminary injunctions; its effect as a bar to accounting; how and when to set up laches and how lapse of time alone is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: laches as defense in equity (591, 596); defense to preliminary injunction (684); as bar to accounting (644); how guarded against (597); setting up laches (597); laches in interferences (141a, 141c); lapse of time alone does not sustain defense (596).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses (formation, scope, defenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and effects of licenses: express and implied licenses, duration, assignability, recording, restrictions (price/use), surrender, implied incidents, licenses as defense to injunctions and how pleaded/proved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: licenses arising from acquiescence/estoppel/recovery; construction of licenses (306); defined (274, 296); express with/without implied incidents (297-302); implied from conduct/employment (311-313a); may be granted after application (303); notice of licenses and recording (304); price and use restrictions (314a et seq.); how pleaded in law/equity (465, 618); surrender and forfeiture (308-309).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of Actions / Time
rubrics_metrics.description: Statute of limitations and other time limitations relevant to initiating actions, bills of review, bills of revivor, and timing for reissue or preliminary injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to relevant sections for beginning actions (472, 476, 477), bills of review (651, 652), bills of revivor (627), lapse of time before applying for broadened reissue (226, 227), and timing before motions for preliminary injunctions (684).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking 'Patented' (effect and proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of marking patented articles, proof and pleading requirements, and its role in recovering damages or profits versus obtaining injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be shown to recover damages or profits (579); need not be shown to obtain an injunction (636); making/selling without marking how far a defense in equity and how pleaded and proved (463, 616, 528); method of marking (496); must be negatived in plaintiff's pleading/evidence where applicable (433a, 496).

rubrics_metrics.name: Means (claim drafting / claim language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and interpretation of the word 'means' in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed reference to use of the word in claims (117a); relevant to claim construction and means-plus-function analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of Operation (effect on infringement and novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of mode of operation in specifications, its effect on infringement inquiries, and when novelty of mode is necessary for invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: mode of operation described in specifications (111); affects infringement (341-346a); novelty of mode when necessary to invention (37); change by omission of parts (35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials (substitution effects on invention and infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: How substitution of materials affects invention and infringement inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitution of materials as affecting infringement (370-372) and invention (28-29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Models (evidence and requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of physical models in patent practice: when required, meaning, evidentiary significance, and effect on novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making of models may constitute evidence of conception/reduction to practice (70, 141a); meaning of 'model' (61); models never negative of novelty (61); when required with applications (127); amendment of models (138, 214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multifariousness and Multiplicity of Suits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on joining multiple patents/claims in a single bill, multifarious pleadings, and preventing multiplicity of suits (e.g., dealers vs manufacturers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries address bills declaring on joint and separate infringements (407), bills in equity joining patents (417), multiplicity of suits against dealers while suit pending against manufacturer (70), and when multiple patents may be joined in one bill (417).

rubrics_metrics.name: New Matter in Reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition or meaning of 'new matter' in reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry: new matter in reissues (214) and meaning of the phrase (240); relevant to reissue practice and correctness of surrender/reenforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (what negates and what does not)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive list of what constitutes prior art that negates novelty (prior patents, printed publications, prior use/sale, foreign patents/publications under certain conditions) and what does not negate novelty (forgotten arts, models, incomplete prior descriptions, private foreign patents, later patents bearing earlier application date, unpublished drawings, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subentries: defined (53); must be put in issue in declarations (424); necessary to patentability (52); negatived by prior knowledge/use/making/printed publication/prior patent (various citations 54-57, 71-72, 93-104a); not negatived by ignorance of anticipating matter (73), forgotten acts (71), prior model (61), incomplete description (57), later patent with earlier application date (55), prior private foreign patent (55), unpublished drawings (61), prior useless process/thing (65), etc.; evidence of want of novelty and degree of proof required (506-509, 76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Use (of patent) and its consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-use of a patent as a ground for narrow construction of claims and its (limited) effect as a defense in equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-use grounds narrow construction of claims (185); non-use is not a defense in equity generally (701a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice (constructive and actual) and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive notice of letters patent, notice of infringement, licenses, and relevance of notice to remedies and recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive notice to all persons from letters patent (191); notice of infringement and its relation to damages/profits/defenses (528, 579, 596, 636, 644); notice of licenses and recording (304); notice of special matter (443, 444); protecting prior unrecorded assignments (281).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths and affidavits in patent practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of oaths and affirmations to specifications, answers, bills, pleas, and who can administer them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmations substituted for oaths (124); oaths to specifications and who may administer (122, magistrates reference); supplemental oaths (138); oaths to answers and bills in equity (581, 584, 589).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof and evidence standards (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: How various matters must be proved or pleaded in actions at law and in equity: novelty, invention, infringement, identity, licenses, marking, non-use, laches, and other defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous cross-references: how novelty and invention are pleaded and proved (424, 446-447, 505-510); how infringement is pleaded (434-435, 579); proof on motions for preliminary injunctions (676); rules of evidence in interferences (141); how letters patent are proved (129, 506); how licenses are proved (530); proof of marking (528).
